events.title: Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act enacted
events.summary: President Clinton signed the Telecommunications Act of 1996 on February 8, 1996 — including Section 230, which shielded online platforms from liability for user-generated content.
events.about: Section 230 became the legal backbone of social media, forums, and marketplaces: platforms could moderate without becoming publishers of every post. Courts and Congress have debated reform ever since, but the statute enabled YouTube, Reddit, [App Store]s, and comment sections at scale.

narrative.whyChosen: Section 230 defined how the internet could host third-party speech without platform [bankruptcy].
narrative.whyImportant: It let startups scale user content before they could afford armies of lawyers.
narrative.problemSolved: Early online services faced lawsuits for every defamatory or infringing post users published.
